findings.title: Malformed raw FETCH could become false tombstones
findings.resolution: The parser now latches fatal failure and the raw command is failed/aborted; no accepted prefix can become a successful page.

findings.title: Multipart header-only source failed MIME parsing
findings.resolution: Header fetch now requests only envelope fields, excluding MIME content headers that require an omitted body. Full BODY[] fetch remains byte exact.

findings.title: Unbalanced response syntax could print private literal data
findings.resolution: Strict raw parsing rejects unbalanced parentheses/unterminated values; the legacy warning no longer prints literal content.

findings.title: Case-sensitive FETCH atoms could be ignored
findings.resolution: Protocol atoms are compared case-insensitively, with literal bytes untouched.

findings.title: Cancelled connections could complete late or remain open
findings.resolution: Hard abort destroys current sockets and invalidates the connection generation. Generation is checked both around connect completion and after TLS/subscription awaits; late sockets are destroyed.

findings.title: Sparse UID space allowed excessively large whole sweeps
findings.resolution: Whole UID sweeps are explicitly limited to a default ceiling of 10000 (configurable through 100000); larger UIDNEXT/continuation ceilings return unsupported before FETCH. This is an explicit first-slice limitation, not sparse-mailbox scalability.

findings.title: OAUTHBEARER GS2 identity and challenge handling were incorrect
findings.resolution: GS2 uses a=, an error continuation sends AQ==, and both OAuth modes require the advertised mechanism plus SASL-IR before initial-response authentication.

findings.title: Input-budget failures could be mislabeled authentication/transient errors
findings.location: ProtocolResourceLimit, ImapResponseReader, Uint8ListReader, ClientBase greeting handling and _run
findings.resolution: Literal, line, greeting and aggregate response limits latch a typed quota condition; quota classification precedes authentication classification.

findings.title: Acknowledged STORE could report success without desired flags
findings.resolution: Source identity is read before mutation, exact UID flags are re-read after STORE, and MOVE checks source absence. Unsupported MOVE and missing source are rejected before mutation.

findings.title: Final lease invalidation could hide completed-write uncertainty
findings.resolution: The mutation-started state remains latched through final lease checks; any subsequent failure is conflict without automatic retry.

findings.title: Malformed FETCH sequence prefix remained silently ignored
findings.resolution: FETCH-looking data is detected separately, then positive 32-bit sequence syntax is validated. A malformed prefix fails instead of generating a successful empty sync page.

findings.title: Aborting a pending real TLS handshake cannot close detached underlying socket
findings.impact: The provider result can time out or cancel while the real TCP/TLS connection remains open. Generation checks destroy a socket only after the secure future completes, so a peer that never finishes TLS can retain resources across retries. No credential transmission or mutation is claimed in this failure mode.
findings.evidence: tls-sdk-review.json records the pinned Dart 3.13.7 detachment and handshake-future ownership proof. The controlled TLS seam does not model that transfer.
findings.required_resolution: Retain a cancellable raw transport owner during both implicit TLS and STARTTLS, and add a real loopback peer that stalls the handshake; demonstrate closure on timeout/cancellation before marking resolved.

execution_evidence.controlled_tests_status: Authored controls statically inspected. Author reported development passes separately; final root source-bound execution receipt remains required. This reviewer ran no Dart or Flutter.

limitations: The controlled socket fixture exercises actual ClientBase connect/upgrade/abort and enough_mail command/response code, but substitutes socket construction. It does not prove real TLS negotiation, trust-store behavior, certificate hostname rejection, or live account/provider compatibility.
UID sweeps use numeric windows and tombstones for missing UIDs. The explicit ceiling prevents unbounded sparse scans; scalable discovery/CONDSTORE/QRESYNC remains outside this slice.
MOVE success verifies acknowledged command plus source absence, not a returned destination UID mapping. Reconciliation of destination membership remains a later sync responsibility.

Header parsing accepts partial envelope projections because MailHeaderRecord has no diagnostics field; after envelope-only HEADER.FIELDS this is not a demonstrated corruption blocker. Full-message parsing rejects partial results.
No concrete INBOX-case-alias regression was demonstrated; canonicalization was not added as an unsolicited scope expansion.
No live OAuth flow, platform keychain, SMTP sending, background retry, or mailbox-wide expunge is qualified here.

RawImapMessage bytes documentation now identifies BODY[HEADER.FIELDS ...] correctly; byte-copy implementation is unchanged.

The committed README and fork patch notes explicitly separate controlled protocol evidence from real TLS, live OAuth/account interoperability and future large/sparse mailbox pagination.
The complete changed-path manifest includes formatter-only existing Mail core/store tests and package/fork documentation, in addition to transport and fork implementation files.
